evals.prompt: I run a 6-person landscaping company. I want a small web app where crews log hours and materials per job from their phones, I approve timesheets weekly, and at month end I export hours per client as a CSV for invoicing in QuickBooks (just the CSV, no integration). Crew members only see their own entries; my office manager can edit anyone's entries but can't approve. I'm slammed this week — don't interview me, make reasonable calls and write the requirements doc.
evals.expected_output: A requirements package with stable IDs, testable ACs, labeled assumptions and a clear out-of-scope, written without interviewing
assertions: Requirements docs are written under docs/requirements/
Every user story has a stable US-n ID and every acceptance criterion an AC-n.m ID
At least 80% of acceptance criteria are Given/When/Then or contain a concrete value
Business rules have BR-n IDs and include both 'office manager can edit but not approve' and 'crew see only their own entries'
Guessed decisions are listed in a separate Assumptions section, not presented as decided
Out of Scope explicitly excludes a QuickBooks integration (CSV only)
No technical decisions (frameworks, databases, API styles) appear outside a constraints/preferences section
Failure or edge states are covered (e.g. rejected timesheet, edits after approval, offline or missing data)
